newsitem.title: USA: Zenith Q3 hurt by severance, writeoffs.
newsitem.headline: Zenith Q3 hurt by severance, writeoffs.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp said Friday that executive severance, consulting fees and writeoffs associated with inventories and receivables contributed to its loss for the third-quarter.

The consumer electronics and network systems company reported a loss of $40.2 million or $0.61 per share versus a year-earlier profit of $1.8 million or $0.04 per share which included a $7.5 million tax credit.
While overall sales advanced, gross margins were down due to lower selling prices and delays in new model shipments for higher-margin consumer electronics products, Zenith said.
In late August, Albin Moschner resigned as president and chief executive officer. The company named Peter Willmott as an interim replacement while it seeks a permanent successor.

Zenith said its higher consumer electronics revenues were driven largely by higher VCR sales. The company's domestic direct-view color television unit sales were flat compared with the 1995 quarter, while industry color TV unit sales to dealers declined.
Zenith's sales of color picture tubes to other manufacturers were down in the quarter. International and commercial products sales also gained.

Network systems revenues were down significantly in the quarter compared with a year ago because of slowing industrywide demand for analog set-top boxes as cable operators prepare to launch digital networks.

Industry and Zenith shipments of cable modems, while still relatively small, rose in the 1996 quarter. During the quarter, Zenith signed a five-year agreement with the Americast programming venture to provide up to three million digital set-top boxes to telecommunications companies. Initial shiments under this contract are expected to begin in mid-1997.
